To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of N = 1 orientifolds is limited to a finite set, (2) the orientifold theories that possess a well defined world-sheet limit are the same as those that have a large N gauge coupling limit, and (3) the world-sheet description in the large N gauge coupling region reduces to the N = 4 parent theory.

(i) the orientifold gauge theories obtained via the orientifolds of Abelian C/ Γ orbifolds that possess well defined world sheet description, (ii) have the property that their large N limit computations reduce to the corresponding computations in the parent N=4 theories, (iii) are limited to a rather small number of examples, and (iv) are consistent with the expectations from the field theory.

the orientifold gauge theories with well defined world-sheet descriptions have the property that the computation of any M-point correlation function in these gauge theories reduces in the large N-limit to the corresponding computation of the parent N =4 oriented theory.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the large N gauge theories obtained by orientifold projections of Type II string theory compactified on toroidal orbifold spaces.
the study of four dimensional N =1 supersymmetric gauge theory obtained via orientifold of Type IIB string theory on C/Γ orbifold, where Γ is the Abelian group of discrete symmetries.
the construction and study of four-dimensional N = 1 gauge theories that arise from Type IIB orientifold compactifications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the world-sheet description of Type IIB orientifold gauge theories is inadequate in the presence of non-perturbatively (from the orbifold viewpoint) generated states.
the large N gauge theories that are obtained by orientifold projection of the N = 4 SYM theory on C/Γ are the only ones with a consistent stringy description.

the world-sheet description of the orientifold gauge theories is valid only when the orientifold projection is such that the orientifold gauge group does not have a non-trivial embedding in the parent SU ( N ) gauge group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have constructed all N = 1 four dimensional supersymmetric gauge theories that can be obtained from the Type IIB string theory on an Abelian orbifold.
the world-sheet description of four dimensional Type I orientifolds on toroidal orbifold is rather limited.
we find that in the large limit the orientifold gauge theories are completely determined by the corresponding N = 4 gauge theory and the orbifold data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in the large-N limit, the orientifold gauge theories have the property that the correlation functions in them can be computed by a simple modification of the corresponding computation in N = 4 theory, where the only change is the insertion of a single orientifold plane in the world-sheet diagram.
the large N gauge theories arising from Type IIB orientifold on Abelian orbifolds are very special.
in the large-N limit orientifold gauge theories are equivalent to their parent N = 1 theories.
